decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “basics (add, edit, delete, list bookmarks)” and default “Add / edit / delete bookmarks.” Round 1 client requests the sensible defaults without contesting save or delete.
decisions.note: The proposed basic save and delete capabilities conform at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “Notes/description per bookmark,” while its default editable fields are only “URL, title, description, tags.” Round 1 client selects “notes.”
decisions.note: The client selects the conforming alternative that includes the bookmark note field at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “Tags or folders for organizing.” Round 1 client says, “Please include tags.”
decisions.note: The alternatives differ in fulfillment of tag assignment; the client selects the reference-conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defaults to “filter by tag.” Round 1 client asks to include tags and tag-capable search.
decisions.note: A specific-tag filtering capability is presented conformingly at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker initially proposes only “Search by text and filter by tag.” Round 1 client requires “exact phrases, and combinations such as AND/OR/NOT.”
decisions.note: The client extends the underspecified search proposal with reference-required phrase and Boolean behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes auto-fetching only “page title & favicon.” Round 1 client states that saving must collect “title, description, icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the complete reference metadata set in place of the partial proposal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions auto-fetching but does not state that fetched metadata remains editable. Round 1 client adds “while letting me edit them.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly adds editability of auto-collected metadata at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defaults to a “Favorite toggle.” Round 1 client says, “use ‘read later’ … rather than favorites.”
decisions.note: The client replaces the non-reference favorite behavior with the expected read-later state.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defaults to favorites and only offers archive as an option. Round 1 client says, “use ‘read later’ and archive rather than favorites.”
decisions.note: The client corrects the state model by requiring archive support.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker asks whether to include “Import/export (e.g. browser HTML export)” but omits it from the stated defaults. Round 1 client says, “Please include … import/export.”
decisions.note: The client selects the reference-conforming inclusion of browser-format import and export.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s default feature list has no sorting. Round 1 client requests “sorting.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing list-sorting requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed defaults contain no multi-selection or bulk operations. Round 1 client requests “bulk actions.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing bulk-action capability, though not the whole-filter variant.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s defaults do not address duplicate URLs. Round 1 client states, “Duplicate URLs should open the existing bookmark for editing.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the reference-conforming duplicate-save rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed scope omits saved searches. Round 1 client adds, “I’d also like saved searches.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing reusable saved-filter capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed scope omits snapshots. Round 1 client requests “page snapshots for long-term reference.”
decisions.note: The client adds local page preservation at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s defaults omit profile display settings. Round 1 client requests “display preferences such as default sorting and font size.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing personal display settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes “a clean, modern card/list UI.” Round 1 client selects “A clean, readable list.”
decisions.note: The selected readability-first list presentation is functionally conforming; card versus list styling is otherwise an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Read-later … Two states per bookmark, each a sidebar view with live counts.” Round 2 client says the “read-later … views … sound sufficient.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation presentation provides a read-later state and a separate view.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker describes a read-later state/view and a bulk “read-later” action, but never states how a bookmark is marked read and removed from that view. Round 2 client only says the view sounds sufficient.
decisions.note: Implementation review leaves the mark-read transition unspecified, so divergence cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents archive as a bookmark state with its own sidebar view. Round 2 client says the “archive views … sound sufficient.”
decisions.note: The revised presentation conformingly includes archive state and a separate archived-bookmark view.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker mentions an archive sidebar and an `is:archived` query but does not state whether archived bookmarks are excluded from the default list and ordinary searches. The client gives only general approval.
decisions.note: The archive-exclusion business rule remains unspecified at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists archive and delete as separate actions but does not state that archive is reversible and delete permanent. Round 2 client says archive is sufficient without addressing this distinction.
decisions.note: The presentation does not establish the required lifecycle semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Free-form tags (join table) + private notes” and verified create/edit behavior. Round 2 client says the organization sounds sufficient.
decisions.note: Tag assignment and note storage/editing are conformingly presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says only “Free-form tags”; it neither presents nor rules out existing-tag autocomplete. Round 2 client generally approves organization without mentioning suggestions.
decisions.note: Autocomplete behavior cannot be established from the implementation presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “private notes” but does not say notes accept Markdown or render as Markdown. Round 2 client generally approves organization.
decisions.note: The richer Markdown-note behavior remains unspecified.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists multiple sort keys and a “default-sort preference,” plus default view and font size. Round 2 client says the result does what they need.
decisions.note: Sorting and the presented display preferences conform at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defines bulk actions as “read-later / archive / add-tags / delete,” omitting remove-tags and an explicit mark-read action. Round 2 client says “bulk actions … sound sufficient” without identifying these differences.
decisions.note: The final bulk-action set is incomplete relative to the reference; the response is category-level approval, not explicit acceptance of the omissions.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies “Select rows” for bulk actions and never offers application to the whole currently filtered collection. Round 2 client says bulk actions sound sufficient without mentioning this scope difference.
decisions.note: Only selected-row bulk operations are presented; the whole-filter action is missing and passes without correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “browser Netscape HTML” import/export alongside JSON and reports Netscape HTML import verification. Round 2 client says import/export sounds sufficient.
decisions.note: The additional JSON format is orthogonal; Netscape HTML support conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “A real boolean parser,” AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, implicit AND, and quoted phrases, with a verification example. Round 2 client says search sounds sufficient.
decisions.note: Boolean grouping and exact-phrase search conform in the revised presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents tag-search syntax as `tag:work`, while the reference requires `#tag`. Round 2 client says search sounds sufficient but does not identify or explicitly accept the syntax difference.
decisions.note: The documented tag-query syntax departs from the reference and receives only bare feature approval.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker demonstrates query parsing but does not state that text search covers title, description, note, and URL or that matching is case-insensitive. Round 2 client only says search sounds sufficient.
decisions.note: The presented evidence cannot establish conformity or divergence for search fields and case handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says metadata fetching pulls title, description, icon, and preview information and that “all fields stay editable.” Round 2 client says the app does what they need.
decisions.note: The revised metadata collection and editability decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker states, “On add/fetch, a matching URL opens the existing bookmark for editing instead of duplicating.” Round 2 client accepts the result.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save behavior exactly conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents saved searches that “Store query + view + sort under a name”; the query language supports included and negated tags. Round 2 client says saved searches sound sufficient.
decisions.note: Saving the reusable query, including tag conditions encoded in it, is functionally equivalent to the reference bundle.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says Playwright stores “saved HTML per bookmark,” with a screenshot as an additional artifact. Round 2 client says snapshots sound sufficient.
decisions.note: For ordinary web pages, retaining local HTML conforms; the additional screenshot is not itself a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker describes the snapshot path generically as Playwright screenshot plus saved HTML “per bookmark” and does not provide the required PDF-download exception. Round 2 client says snapshots sound sufficient without identifying the PDF difference.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation applies the page-capture approach without the reference’s PDF-specific storage behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s complete snapshot description provides only local Playwright capture; no Internet Archive snapshot option is presented. Round 2 client says snapshots sound sufficient without stating or accepting that difference.
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation is absent from the presented snapshot solution and passes without an explicit response.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Default sort, default view, font size.” Round 2 client says the application does what they need.
decisions.note: The implementation review presents conforming display-related settings.
